question: Assume today is 2026-10-27. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of net mortgage approvals for house purchase in the United Kingdom in September 2026 (seasonally adjusted), as it will be first reported in the Bank of England's monthly Money and Credit statistical release.

target.what: Number of net mortgage approvals for house purchase in the United Kingdom in September 2026, seasonally adjusted, as first reported by the Bank of England in its monthly Money and Credit statistical release
target.unit: net mortgage approvals for house purchase, seasonally adjusted
target.caveats: Net approvals are approvals net of cancellations and cover house purchase only, excluding remortgaging; the series is seasonally adjusted and UK-wide. The target is the first print for September 2026, which may be revised later. If the September 2026 Money and Credit release is published after the 2

candidates.hypothesis: The target's own recent history and September seasonality provide the primary anchor: September 2026 approvals should be close to the recent seasonally adjusted level adjusted by the historical September seasonal factor. Route: target ≈ recent 3-month average × historical September factor, with recent trend adjustment.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly Bank of England Money and Credit net mortgage approvals for house purchase, seasonally adjusted, from January 2023 through August 2026; especially September 2023, September 2024, September 2025, and the latest August 2026 print and revisions. Minimum evidence: the latest 6-12 monthly SA observations and at least 3 prior September values.

candidates.hypothesis: Mortgage approvals for house purchase co-move with remortgage approvals and are negatively related to new mortgage effective interest rates. August 2026 remortgage approvals, net mortgage lending, and effective rates can constrain the September 2026 house purchase approvals level. Route: target ≈ f(remortgage approvals, effective new mortgage rate change, net lending).
candidates.data_to_find: Bank of England Money and Credit series for net mortgage approvals for remortgage, net mortgage lending, and effective interest rate on new mortgages, monthly through August 2026; Bank Rate and 2-year/5-year swap rates around September 2026. Minimum evidence: latest 3-6 months of remortgage approvals and effective rates.

candidates.hypothesis: Residential property transactions are an administrative trace of completed housing activity. Although approvals lead completions, the recent level and trend in HMRC transactions and stamp duty receipts can validate whether the housing market was stronger or weaker in September 2026. Route: use transactions trend to adjust the approvals forecast, not as a direct one-to-one substitute.
candidates.data_to_find: HMRC monthly UK residential property transactions, seasonally adjusted, for September 2026 and recent months; stamp duty land tax receipts if available. Minimum evidence: September 2026 HMRC transaction count and the prior 6 months.

candidates.hypothesis: Buyer demand and agreed sales lead mortgage approvals. RICS new buyer enquiries and agreed sales, plus the Bank of England Credit Conditions Survey demand balance for secured lending, should indicate the direction and magnitude of September 2026 approvals relative to recent months. Route: target ≈ recent approvals level adjusted by survey demand surprise.

assessment.note: August 2026 approvals at 54,900 and July at 55,900 are repeated across BoE/press/TE copies. They are the same underlying Money and Credit series and do not provide independent confirmation.
The six-month average of about 60,100 is repeated from the same BoE release; useful as a level benchmark but not independent.
September 2026 consensus at about 54,300 appears in several copies of the same Trading Economics/consensus lineage; they should count as one forecast signal, not multiple independent polls.
Trading Economics model forecast at about 54,500 is a second forecast on the same calendar family and is correlated with the consensus.

The credible pre-release forecasts cluster near 54,300-54,500. The 59,100 end-Q3 model projection is stale relative to the September forecast, while the claimed September actual/consensus of 55,000/56,000 is impossible before the first BoE September print and conflicts with the release schedule.
Official RICS September survey shows new buyer enquiries at -22 (down from -18) and agreed sales at -18 (down from -16), repeated across several reports from the same RICS survey.

These items are dated 11 September but report RICS September figures. Their values match the August RICS readings (e.g. -19 and -17) and conflict with the official September RICS release (-22 and -18). They are period-mislabeled and should not be used as September evidence.

BoE Q3 2026 Credit Conditions Survey reports sharply negative past demand for secured house-purchase lending, weaker remortgage demand, reduced secured credit availability, and a lower approvals share. p131 is a duplicate of the availability finding.
The effective interest rate on newly drawn mortgages rose from 4.45% in July to 4.60% in August. Copies share the same BoE Money and Credit source.

Mortgage-rate and product evidence points to a September tightening: two-year fixed rates around 5.59% in September, the Moneyfacts average new mortgage rate rising from 5.55% on 25 August to 5.83% on 25 September, and sub-5% fixed deals collapsing. These are different market indicators but all support a negative September demand shock.

HMRC August 2026 seasonally adjusted residential transactions were 95,220, down about 1% on July. These are copies of the same HMRC administrative series, and they reflect completions from earlier agreed sales rather than September approvals directly.
Bank Rate was held at 3.75% on 17 September 2026 by a 6-3 vote. These are the same MPC decision reported by several outlets.

methods.rationale: Own-history benchmark using first-print target values around 2025-26. Because the kept monthly series has gaps and fewer than 13 consecutive months, the code's fallback anchors on September 2025 and recent June-August year-on-year changes. This captures the persistent level and downward trend but not any September-specific rate shock; it shares BoE first-print vintage and revision risk.

methods.rationale: Carries the August 2026/August 2025 year-on-year ratio into September 2025's level, then applies a2 for the observed September rate and demand deterioration. This is a transparent year-on-year carry route. Shared dependence on first-print target history and the assumption that August-to-September relative YoY change is stable enough; it fails if September deviated sharply from August's relationship.

methods.rationale: Uses the recent three-month average as the local level and adjusts it using the September RICS weakening, the BoE Credit Conditions Survey's very negative past-demand and availability balances, and the observed rise in mortgage rates. It shares dependence on the recent BoE prints and on the judgemental survey-to-approvals mapping; it fails if the survey signal overstates or understates September approvals.

methods.rationale: Uses the pre-cutoff consensus and Trading Economics model forecast, which should incorporate available high-frequency housing, mortgage-rate, and lender data. The two forecasts share the same Trading Economics calendar family and are not independent confirmation; the route fails if the consensus is stale or based on a different definition than the BoE first print.

assumptions.name: September 2026 approvals relative to June-August 2026 average
assumptions.rationale: September demand indicators weakened: RICS new buyer enquiries fell to -22 from -18 and agreed sales to -18 from -16; BoE Q3 2026 Credit Conditions Survey showed a -37.1 past-demand balance for secured house-purchase lending and reduced secured credit availability (-15.5); the effective new mortgage rate rose to 4.60% in August and quoted fixed rates rose through September. The pre-cutoff consensus (54.3k) and TE forecast (54.5k) sit roughly 3.5% below the June-August average of the kept approvals prints, implying a factor near 0.965. The wide range allows for mapping error from surveys and rates to approvals.
assumptions.applies_when: The June-August 2026 average is a usable local baseline and September survey/rate weakness shifts the level proportionally rather than causing a structural break.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that September buyer demand rebounded strongly, mortgage rates fell materially during September, or the first print came in near the 60k six-month average.

assumptions.name: September 2026 year-on-year change relative to August 2026 year-on-year change
assumptions.rationale: August 2026 approvals were about 84.9% of August 2025; simply carrying that year-on-year ratio into September would ignore the further September rate shock. The Moneyfacts average new mortgage rate rose from 5.55% on 25 August to 5.83% on 25 September, two-year fixed rates rose through September, and sub-5% deals collapsed. The 54.3k September consensus is consistent with a September year-on-year ratio about 2-3% weaker than August's. The range allows for the possibility that August was the low point.
assumptions.applies_when: The August year-on-year decline is a reasonable starting point and September's incremental rate/demand shock is a proportional adjustment.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that September approvals stabilized near the August year-on-year ratio or that the rate shock did not affect approvals volumes.

a3.role: dimensionless factor for September 2026 net house-purchase approvals relative to September 2025, incorporating the recent year-on-year decline and September 2026 demand/rate conditions

methods.rationale: Year-on-year level-scaling route anchored directly on the same month last year. It avoids the invalid August 2025 denominator and uses p16 as the prior-year count with a3 as the dimensionless change factor. Main risks are revisions to the September 2025 base, the exact September seasonal residual despite seasonal adjustment, and rate-transmission lags. It shares BoE source dependence with m3 and consensus calibration through a3.

methods.rationale: Recent-level route: the June-August 2026 average of first-print net house-purchase approvals, adjusted by a survey-and-rate factor. The recent three-month average is a BoE anchor; the adjustment reflects weaker RICS buyer enquiries/agreed sales, weak BoE Credit Conditions demand and availability, and tighter mortgage rates/product shelf-life. It is partly correlated with m2 through the BoE source and consensus context, but it uses the recent three-month level rather than a pure year-on-year rule.

assumptions.name: September 2026 approvals adjustment relative to the June-August 2026 average
assumptions.rationale: September 2026 demand indicators weakened: RICS buyer enquiries fell to -22% and agreed sales to -18%, BoE Credit Conditions Q3 2026 past secured-lending demand was -37.1 and availability -15.5, and mortgage rates/product shelf-life tightened. The published consensus is a little below the June-August average, so a modest downward adjustment is central, with a wide range for transmission lags and residual seasonality.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to adjust the June-August 2026 average of first-print net house-purchase approvals to September 2026 conditions.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that RICS/CCS weakness did not transmit to approvals, or that mortgage rates fell or product availability expanded enough to offset the weakening.

assumptions.name: September 2026 net house-purchase approvals relative to September 2025
assumptions.rationale: September 2025 net house-purchase approvals were 65,900. Through 2026 the monthly level has fallen to 54.9k-58.2k, and the published September 2026 consensus is around 54.3k, implying a ratio near 0.82-0.83 to September 2025. RICS and Credit Conditions evidence points to slightly weaker September than summer, so a wide range is retained for revisions and rate-lag uncertainty.
assumptions.applies_when: Used as a year-on-year change factor applied to the September 2025 net house-purchase approvals level.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 approvals held near or above the summer 2026 level, or that the September 2025 base is materially revised.

methods.label: m2

p16.role: UK net mortgage approvals for house purchase, seasonally adjusted, September 2025, first print from the 29 October 2025 Money and Credit release, count in the month

a3.role: dimensionless factor for September 2026 net house-purchase approvals relative to September 2025, incorporating the recent year-on-year decline and September 2026 demand/rate conditions

methods.rationale: Year-on-year level-scaling route anchored directly on the same month last year. It avoids the invalid August 2025 denominator and uses p16 as the prior-year count with a3 as the dimensionless change factor. Main risks are revisions to the September 2025 base, the exact September seasonal residual despite seasonal adjustment, and rate-transmission lags. It shares BoE source dependence with m3 and c

The best estimate for net mortgage approvals for house purchase in the United Kingdom in September 2026, seasonally adjusted, as first reported by the Bank of England, is [[estimate]] [[unit]] ([[interval_level]] interval [[p10]] to [[p90]] [[unit]]).

Two routes were combined with equal weight per block: a year-on-year level-scaling route ([[m1_estimate]] [[unit]], weight [[m1_weight]]) multiplying the September 2025 observed level [[p16_value]] by an assumed ratio [[a3_value]] (range [[a3_low]] to [[a3_high]]); and a recent-level route ([[m2_estimate]] [[unit]], weight [[m2_weight]]) averaging observed June-August prints [[p197_value]], [[p2_value]] and [[p1_value]], adjusted by an assumed factor [[a1_value]] (range [[a1_low]] to [[a1_high]]). The combination is a geometric mean of the two blocks; the interval is conditional on those assumptions.

The main risk is that the assumed September adjustment and year-on-year ratio are wrong, since both rest on survey and rate evidence rather than observed September data. The most useful missing evidence would be early September approvals or a firmer published consensus.

Unit of the estimate: [[unit_full]].

Key assumptions (proposed by the analyst model, not observed; code samples each one between the bounds shown):
- a1 September 2026 approvals adjustment relative to the June-August 2026 average: [[a1_value]] ratio, range [[a1_low]] to [[a1_high]] (range widened by code); used by m2. Overturned by: Evidence that RICS/CCS weakness did not transmit to approvals, or that mortgage rates fell or product availability expanded enough to offset the weakening.
- a3 September 2026 net house-purchase approvals relative to September 2025: [[a3_value]] ratio, range [[a3_low]] to [[a3_high]] (range widened by code); used by m1. Overturned by: Evidence that September 2026 approvals held near or above the summer 2026 level, or that the September 2025 base is materially revised.

Method details (computed by code):
- m1 formula_mc: p16 * a3; Monte Carlo P10 to P90 [[m1_mc_p10]] to [[m1_mc_p90]]; result unit (approval/month) * 1 month converted to approval; own 80% width [[m1_width]] (Monte Carlo of the formula inputs)
- m2 formula_mc: mean(p1, p2, p197) * a1; Monte Carlo P10 to P90 [[m2_mc_p10]] to [[m2_mc_p90]]; result unit (approval/month) * 1 month converted to approval; own 80% width [[m2_width]] (Monte Carlo of the formula inputs)
- Combination: [[n_blocks]] block(s), equal weight per block (methods whose inputs overlap by at least half form one block; backtest errors set widths, not weights): B1 = m1: [[block1_value]] (width [[block1_width]], Monte Carlo of the formula inputs); B2 = m2: [[block2_value]] (width [[block2_width]], Monte Carlo of the formula inputs). Estimate = the geometric mean of the two blocks.
- Interval: root mean square of the block widths [[blocks_rms_width]]; Birge ratio [[birge_ratio]] (not above one, so no widening); final width [[final_width]].
final.text:
The best estimate for net mortgage approvals for house purchase in the United Kingdom in September 2026, seasonally adjusted, as first reported by the Bank of England, is 54,348 approval (80% model-based interval 37,184 to 79,436 approval).

Two routes were combined with equal weight per block: a year-on-year level-scaling route (54,012 approval, weight 50%) multiplying the September 2025 observed level 65,900 net mortgage approvals for house purchase by an assumed ratio 0.825 (range 0.5821 to 1.164); and a recent-level route (54,687 approval, weight 50%) averaging observed June-August prints 58,200 net mortgage approvals for house purchase, 55,900 net mortgage approvals for house purchase and 54,900 net mortgage approvals for house purchase, adjusted by an assumed factor 0.965 (range 0.6803 to 1.361). The combination is a geometric mean of the two blocks; the interval is conditional on those assumptions.

The main risk is that the assumed September adjustment and year-on-year ratio are wrong, since both rest on survey and rate evidence rather than observed September data. The most useful missing evidence would be early September approvals or a firmer published consensus.

Unit of the estimate: approval (net mortgage approvals for house purchase, seasonally adjusted; total for 2026-09-01 to 2026-09-30).

Key assumptions (proposed by the analyst model, not observed; code samples each one between the bounds shown):
- a1 September 2026 approvals adjustment relative to the June-August 2026 average: 0.965 ratio, range 0.6803 to 1.361 (range widened by code); used by m2. Overturned by: Evidence that RICS/CCS weakness did not transmit to approvals, or that mortgage rates fell or product availability expanded enough to offset the weakening.
- a3 September 2026 net house-purchase approvals relative to September 2025: 0.825 ratio, range 0.5821 to 1.164 (range widened by code); used by m1. Overturned by: Evidence that September 2026 approvals held near or above the summer 2026 level, or that the September 2025 base is materially revised.

Method details (computed by code):
- m1 formula_mc: p16 * a3; Monte Carlo P10 to P90 36,584 to 80,517; result unit (approval/month) * 1 month converted to approval; own 80% width x/÷1.48 (Monte Carlo of the formula inputs)
- m2 formula_mc: mean(p1, p2, p197) * a1; Monte Carlo P10 to P90 37,909 to 78,513; result unit (approval/month) * 1 month converted to approval; own 80% width x/÷1.44 (Monte Carlo of the formula inputs)
- Combination: 2 block(s), equal weight per block (methods whose inputs overlap by at least half form one block; backtest errors set widths, not weights): B1 = m1: 54,012 (width x/÷1.48, Monte Carlo of the formula inputs); B2 = m2: 54,687 (width x/÷1.44, Monte Carlo of the formula inputs). Estimate = the geometric mean of the two blocks.
- Interval: root mean square of the block widths x/÷1.46; Birge ratio 0.03 (not above one, so no widening); final width x/÷1.46.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
